threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for directions to the nearest station, while everyone else just knows to head to the overground.
Caught a whiff of jerk chicken from a food truck on the 59 last night, and the driver rolled his eyes at the waiting crowd like it was all part of the show.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh döner mingling with the sound of a nearby street musician playing a medieval lute. That’s when I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a doner at 3 AM after a night out, served by the same guy who knows your order by heart. That's community.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell when someone’s from here; they know you should never trust a BART schedule after 5 PM. It's like playing Russian roulette on the Transbay Tube.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 49 pulling a full drum set while complaining about the 5-minute delay. Only in SF would that make sense.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think they can find tapas in any corner, but real locals know to seek out the quiet bars where the menú del dia isn't plastered on the wall.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their fascination with the street performers at plaça del Sol, snapping endless photos while locals just pass by.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's weird to see someone busking with an accordion on a Tuesday afternoon at Dalston Junction.
Heard a couple argue about whose turn it was to pay for a kebab on the 36, while the driver pretended not to hear the chaos.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw my neighbor chasing after the BVG bus wearing slippers, yelling about missing the line 171. That's Neukölln life in action.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the kebab shops here never close? It’s like they have a secret pact to fuel the night owls—best at 3 AM.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot locals by how they gauge BART delays—timing their coffee runs based on the latest equipment failures. Tourists just look confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in the back of the 49 bus playing a ukelele while a dog sat in a seat watching him like a fan. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always miss that Gràcia shuts down on Sundays; locals flock to the plazas instead, sipping vermut while shops rest. It's a whole different vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their fascination with the 'paseo' culture—always blissfully unaware that the locals are just avoiding the heat.
